components.name: DoorControlSWC
components.description: Controls door lock, unlock, and child-lock actuation based on switch inputs and vehicle speed constraints.

components.name: WindowLiftSWC
components.description: Manages one-touch window lift, anti-pinch protection, and window position learning.

components.name: MirrorAdjustSWC
components.description: Controls mirror folding, heating, and position adjustment requests.

components.name: LightControlSWC
components.description: Controls interior ambient lighting and welcome light sequences.

components.name: SeatAdjustSWC
components.description: Handles seat position and lumbar adjustment requests with memory profiles.

components.name: ClimateInterfaceSWC
components.description: Bridges body domain functions to climate blower and recirculation actuators.

components.name: KeylessEntrySWC
components.description: Processes keyless authentication challenges and unlocks authorization.

components.name: BodyControlSWC
components.description: Central body domain arbiter; resolves actuator command conflicts and applies safety interlocks.

components.name: VehicleModeSWC
components.description: Maintains vehicle mode state (park, drive, crash) and distributes mode changes.

components.name: SpeedProviderSWC
components.description: Provides filtered vehicle speed for anti-pinch and child-lock interlocks.

components.name: RteAdapter
components.description: RTE adapter layer mapping SWC ports onto BSW communication services.

components.name: Com
components.description: AUTOSAR COM module; signal packing, transmission cycles, and timeout monitoring.

components.name: PduR
components.description: PDU router; routes PDUs between COM, CanIf, and transport layers.

components.name: CanIf
components.description: CAN interface; multiplexes PDUs onto CAN controller channels.

components.name: CanDriver
components.description: CAN driver for the body controller CAN channel with hardware filter configuration.

components.name: CanSm
components.description: CAN state manager; coordinates bus-off recovery and channel start/stop.

components.name: NvM
components.description: NVRAM manager; persists window pinch thresholds and seat memory profiles.

components.name: EcuM
components.description: ECU state manager; coordinates startup, shutdown, and sleep transitions.

components.name: DiagManager
components.description: Unified diagnostic services manager for UDS-based diagnostics.

components.name: IoHwAb
components.description: I/O hardware abstraction mapping physical pins to logical signals (door switches, window motors, mirror motors).

dependencies.evidence: The DoorControlSWC requires door lock and unlock commands from the BodyControlSWC.
The WindowLiftSWC requires window lift commands from the BodyControlSWC.
The MirrorAdjustSWC requires mirror adjustment commands from the BodyControlSWC.
The SeatAdjustSWC requires seat adjustment commands from the BodyControlSWC.
The ClimateInterfaceSWC requires blower control authorization from the BodyControlSWC.
The BodyControlSWC requires vehicle mode information from the VehicleModeSWC before releasing actuator commands.
The BodyControlSWC requires filtered vehicle speed from the SpeedProviderSWC for anti-pinch interlocks.
The WindowLiftSWC requires vehicle speed to qualify one-touch window operation.
The DoorControlSWC requires keyless authorization status from the KeylessEntrySWC.
The RteAdapter depends on the COM module for signal transmission.
The COM module depends on the PduR for PDU routing.
The PduR depends on the CanIf for CAN transmission.
The CanIf depends on the CanDriver for hardware access.
The CanSm requires bus state control of the CanDriver.
The WindowLiftSWC requires NVRAM persistence of anti-pinch thresholds from the NvM.
The SeatAdjustSWC requires NVRAM persistence of memory profiles from the NvM.
The EcuM requires communication channel control from the CanSm during shutdown.
The EcuM requires COM transmission suspension during shutdown.
The DiagManager requires the RteAdapter for diagnostic read access to application data.
The DoorControlSWC requires raw door switch inputs from the IoHwAb.
The WindowLiftSWC requires window motor current feedback from the IoHwAb.
The MirrorAdjustSWC requires mirror motor feedback from the IoHwAb.
The LightControlSWC requires ambient light feedback from the IoHwAb.
The SeatAdjustSWC requires seat motor feedback from the IoHwAb.

flows.name: Door Lock Actuation
flows.description: Raw switch input is debounced in IoHwAb, evaluated by DoorControlSWC, arbitrated by BodyControlSWC, and the resulting command is transmitted over CAN.

flows.name: One-Touch Window Lift with Anti-Pinch
flows.description: Motor current from IoHwAb is monitored by WindowLiftSWC; vehicle speed from SpeedProviderSWC qualifies the command; BodyControlSWC arbitrates and forwards the request over CAN.

flows.name: Keyless Unlock
flows.description: KeylessEntrySWC publishes the authentication result; BodyControlSWC authorizes the unlock; DoorControlSWC actuates via IoHwAb.

flows.name: Seat Memory Recall
flows.description: NvM provides the persisted profile, SeatAdjustSWC computes motor targets, BodyControlSWC arbitrates, and IoHwAb drives the seat motors.

flows.name: Bus-Off Recovery
flows.description: CanDriver reports the fault, CanSm executes the recovery sequence, and EcuM is informed for mode bookkeeping.

expected_findings.description: Dependency DEP-19 (DiagManager -> RteAdapter) present in v1 is absent in v2 with no replacement.
IF-12 consumer list references old component name VehicleModeSWC after rename to VehicleModeMgrSWC.
VehicleSpeedIF (IF-13) has conflicting provider statements: table says C-08, prose says C-10.
SeatAdjustSWC (C-05) has no interfaces, dependencies, or flows in v2.
IF-11 prose still describes KeyAuthStatus (SG-015) although the signal was removed.
v2 states ClimateInterfaceSWC does not require BodyControlSWC while DEP-05 lists that dependency.
IF-04 prose port count does not match its port table.
WindowStatusIF (IF-03) gained consumer C-04 (LightControlSWC) in v2.

qa_pairs.question: Which component is the central arbiter in the ABC architecture?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: BodyControlSWC (C-08) is the central arbiter; it resolves actuator command conflicts and applies safety interlocks.

qa_pairs.question: Which components provide the VehicleSpeed signal and who consumes it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: SpeedProviderSWC (C-10) provides VehicleSpeedIF (IF-13); consumers are DoorControlSWC (C-01) and WindowLiftSWC (C-02).

qa_pairs.question: What signals are carried by the DoorStatusIF interface?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: DoorStatus (uint8) and ChildLockActive (boolean).

qa_pairs.question: List the components in the CAN communication path in order.
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Application SWC -> RteAdapter (C-11) -> Com (C-12) -> PduR (C-13) -> CanIf (C-14) -> CanDriver (C-15).

qa_pairs.question: Which components depend on the NvM and for what?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: WindowLiftSWC (C-02) persists anti-pinch thresholds; SeatAdjustSWC (C-05) persists memory profiles (DEP-15, DEP-16).

qa_pairs.question: What is the trigger and flow of the Keyless Unlock function?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Trigger: authenticated key approach detected. Flow: KeylessEntrySWC -> BodyControlSWC -> DoorControlSWC -> IoHwAb.

qa_pairs.question: Which interface does WindowLiftSWC provide and which components consume it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: WindowStatusIF (IF-03), consumed by BodyControlSWC (C-08).

qa_pairs.question: What datatype and unit does the WindowPosition signal have?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: uint8, measured in percent (%).

qa_pairs.question: Which components require IoHwAb inputs?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: DoorControlSWC, WindowLiftSWC, MirrorAdjustSWC, LightControlSWC, and SeatAdjustSWC (DEP-20..DEP-24).

qa_pairs.question: How many components are in the Application layer and what are their IDs?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Ten components: C-01 through C-10.

qa_pairs.question: What does the EcuM require from the CanSm?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: During shutdown, EcuM requires communication channel control from the CanSm (DEP-17).

qa_pairs.question: Which flows include the CanDriver?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Door Lock Actuation (FL-1), One-Touch Window Lift (FL-2), and Bus-Off Recovery (FL-5).

qa_pairs.question: What is stored in NVRAM according to the assumptions?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Up to three seat memory profiles per user (assumption A2).

qa_pairs.question: Which interface does the DiagManager use for diagnostic requests?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: DiagRequestIF (IF-22), provided by DiagManager (C-19) and consumed by RteAdapter (C-11).

qa_pairs.question: What safety interlock does the BodyControlSWC apply using vehicle speed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Anti-pinch interlocks: commands are released only when vehicle speed interlocks permit; anti-pinch is mandatory below 5 km/h (A3).

qa_pairs.question: Which signals belong to the IoHwDoorIF interface?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: DoorSwitchRaw (uint8) and WindowMotorCurrent (uint16, mA).

qa_pairs.question: Who consumes the VehicleModeIF interface?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: BodyControlSWC (C-08), DoorControlSWC (C-01), and WindowLiftSWC (C-02).

qa_pairs.question: What happens when the CAN controller enters bus-off?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: CanDriver reports the fault, CanSm executes the recovery sequence, and EcuM is informed (FL-5).

qa_pairs.question: Which component provides the EcuModeIF and who consumes it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Provided by EcuM (C-18); consumed by CanSm (C-16) and Com (C-12).

qa_pairs.question: Describe the Seat Memory Recall flow.
qa_pairs.expected_answer: NvM provides the persisted profile, SeatAdjustSWC computes motor targets, BodyControlSWC arbitrates, IoHwAb drives the seat motors (FL-4).

qa_pairs.question: What is the CAN bus bit rate assumption?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: 500 kbit/s (assumption A1).

qa_pairs.question: Which components communicate over the ComPduRIF?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Com (C-12) provides it; PduR (C-13) consumes it.

qa_pairs.question: How does the Door Lock Actuation flow start and which component debounces the switch input?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: It starts when the driver operates the door lock switch; IoHwAb debounces the raw input (FL-1).

qa_pairs.question: Which dependency IDs link application SWCs to the BodyControlSWC for commands?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: DEP-01 (Door), DEP-02 (Window), DEP-03 (Mirror), DEP-04 (Seat), DEP-05 (Climate).

qa_pairs.question: What does the SpeedProviderSWC do?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: It provides filtered vehicle speed for anti-pinch and child-lock interlocks.

qa_pairs.question: Which interface carries the CanFrame signal?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: PduCanIfIF (IF-17).

qa_pairs.question: What is an R-port and which component has R-ports on VehicleModeIF?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An R-port is a required port; BodyControlSWC, DoorControlSWC, and WindowLiftSWC hold R-ports on VehicleModeIF.

qa_pairs.question: How many signals are in the signal dictionary?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: 34 signals (SG-001 through SG-034).

qa_pairs.question: Which BSW module routes PDUs between COM and CanIf?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: PduR (C-13).

qa_pairs.question: What is out of scope of this HLD?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Detailed timing analysis, AUTOSAR OS configuration, and ECU resource files.

unanswerable_questions.question: What is the brake pressure of the front axle?
unanswerable_questions.reason: Braking system is not part of the body domain HLD.

unanswerable_questions.question: Which AUTOSAR OS task scheduling is configured?
unanswerable_questions.reason: OS configuration is explicitly out of scope (Section 1.2).

unanswerable_questions.question: What is the price of the ABC ECU?
unanswerable_questions.reason: Commercial data is not in an HLD.

unanswerable_questions.question: How is the airbag deployment logic implemented?
unanswerable_questions.reason: Airbag functions are not part of this architecture.

D1_removed_dependency.description: DEP-19 (DiagManager requires RteAdapter) removed in v2 without any replacement path.

D2_stale_component_reference.description: VehicleModeSWC renamed to VehicleModeMgrSWC (C-09), but IF-12 section still references the old name in one table cell.

D3_conflicting_provider.description: IF-13 VehicleSpeedIF claims a second provider (C-08) in its interface table while section text still says C-10.

D4_orphan_component.description: SeatAdjustSWC (C-05) left with no interfaces/dependencies in v2 (all its links removed).

D5_dropped_signal_referenced.description: SG-015 KeyAuthStatus removed from IF-11 in v2, but the IF-11 section text still describes it.

D6_contradictory_statement.description: v2 text states ClimateInterfaceSWC 'does not require any interface from the BodyControlSWC' while DEP-05 remains listed.

D7_port_count_mismatch.description: IF-04 section prose says WindowCommandIF has 2 ports, but its port table lists 3.

D8_new_consumer_of_changed_interface.description: IF-03 WindowStatusIF gains a new consumer C-04 (LightControlSWC) in v2 — impact-relevant change.
